## Q ai-20261022-a12-18
- domain: secure
- task: 1.2
- topic: security
- services: Shield, WAF, CloudFront, ALB, Route 53
- tags: ddos-protection, web-attacks
- difficulty: hard
- skills: 1.2.k6, 1.2.s3
- concept: Shield Advanced adds the Shield Response Team (with Business or Enterprise Support), cost protection, and automatic layer 7 mitigation through a WAF web ACL
- refs: 05-security-services.md
- hint: Cần chuyên gia DDoS 24/7, được hoàn chi phí scale do tấn công, và tự giảm thiểu L7 — gói nào của Shield, và cần gói Support nào?
- status: draft
- created: 2026-10-22
- enriched: 2026-10-22
- time: 130

A gaming company serves players through Amazon Route 53, an Amazon CloudFront distribution, and an internet-facing Application Load Balancer. A large HTTP flood recently made the game unavailable and caused a large scaling bill. The company has an AWS Enterprise Support plan. It wants 24/7 access to AWS DDoS experts during attacks, credits for attack-related scaling costs, and automatic mitigation of layer 7 floods without writing rules during an incident. Which solution will meet these requirements?

- A. Subscribe to AWS Shield Advanced, add the CloudFront distribution and the load balancer as protected resources, and turn on automatic layer 7 DDoS mitigation
- B. Rely on AWS Shield Standard for DDoS protection and create AWS WAF rate-based rules on the CloudFront distribution that block IP addresses above a request threshold
- C. Deploy AWS Network Firewall in the VPC with automatic layer 4 rules that drop traffic from known attacker IP address ranges as DDoS mitigation at the subnet edge
- D. Use AWS Firewall Manager to create security group policies that restrict the load balancer to the CloudFront IP address ranges

**Answer:** A

**Explanation:** Shield Advanced provides access to the Shield Response Team (with Business or Enterprise Support), cost protection through service credits, and automatic layer 7 mitigation that manages WAF rules during an attack.
- Shield Standard with rate-based rules: no expert team, no cost protection, and rules are written by hand (vi phạm ràng buộc)
- Network Firewall in the VPC: not an edge DDoS service and offers neither experts nor credits (dùng sai tính năng)
- Firewall Manager security group policies: restrict the origin but do not mitigate floods (giải bài toán khác)
Docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/ddos-advanced-summary-capabilities.html
> 🇻🇳 DDoS: chuyên gia SRT 24/7 + hoàn chi phí + tự giảm thiểu L7 → Shield Advanced (cần Business/Enterprise Support).

## Q ai-20261022-a12-13
- domain: secure
- task: 1.2
- topic: security
- services: Cognito, S3, IAM
- tags: federation, iam-roles
- difficulty: medium
- skills: 1.2.k4, 1.2.k5
- concept: Cognito user pool authenticates users; an identity pool exchanges the token for temporary credentials scoped by an IAM role policy variable
- refs: 05-security-services.md
- hint: Một thành phần xác thực người dùng, thành phần khác đổi token thành thông tin xác thực tạm thời giới hạn theo từng người dùng.
- status: draft
- created: 2026-10-22
- enriched: 2026-10-22
- time: 145

A photo-sharing startup is building a mobile app. Users sign up with an email address and password. The app must upload each user's photos directly to an Amazon S3 bucket, and each user must be able to reach objects under only their own prefix. The team does not want to run authentication servers or ship long-term AWS credentials inside the app. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose TWO)

- A. Create an Amazon Cognito user pool for sign-up and sign-in, and exchange its tokens for temporary AWS credentials by using a Cognito identity pool
- B. Create an IAM user for each app user and ship the long-term credentials as access keys in the secure storage of the mobile device on each phone
- C. Attach an IAM role to the identity pool that allows object actions under a prefix built with the cognito-identity.amazonaws.com:sub variable
- D. Attach the S3 permissions policy directly to the Cognito user pool so that signed-in users inherit access to their own prefix in the bucket and its objects
- E. Configure a bucket policy that allows uploads from any principal and require the app to use random object names for the photos that it stores

**Answer:** A, C

**Explanation:** The user pool handles sign-up and sign-in, the identity pool trades the token for temporary credentials, and a role policy with the identity ID variable limits each user to a personal prefix.
- IAM user per app user: long-term keys on devices, and this does not scale (vi phạm ràng buộc)
- Policy attached to the user pool: user pools cannot hold IAM permissions (cấu hình không tồn tại)
- Open bucket policy with random names: obscurity is not access control (vi phạm ràng buộc)
Docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/iam-roles.html
> 🇻🇳 User pool = đăng nhập; identity pool = cấp credential tạm; biến ${cognito-identity.amazonaws.com:sub} giới hạn prefix từng user.

- refs: 05-security-services.md

A company has 90 accounts in AWS Organizations. Security requires a baseline AWS WAF web ACL and AWS Shield Advanced protection on every Application Load Balancer and CloudFront distribution, including resources that teams create later and accounts that join the organization later. Non-compliant resources must be remediated automatically with the LEAST operational overhead. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose THREE)

- A. Deploy a CloudFormation StackSet in AWS Organizations that creates a web ACL in each member account and associates it with the load balancers that exist today
- B. Designate a delegated Firewall Manager administrator account for the policies of the organization
- C. Create a service control policy that denies creation of load balancers and distributions that lack an associated web ACL, with automatic remediation of older ones
- D. Enable AWS Config in each member account and Region that is in scope for the Firewall Manager policies
- E. Enable AWS Security Hub in the management account so that it applies the WAF web ACL and Shield Advanced protection to each new resource
- F. Create Firewall Manager AWS WAF and Shield Advanced policies scoped to the organization with automatic remediation turned on

**Explanation:** Firewall Manager needs an administrator account and AWS Config, and its policies keep protecting new resources and new accounts, remediating non-compliant ones automatically.

- Service control policy: cannot evaluate whether a web ACL is associated (dùng sai tính năng)

> 🇻🇳 Bảo vệ tự động toàn tổ chức → Firewall Manager (admin + AWS Config + policy WAF/Shield có auto-remediation).

- domain: cost

- skills: 4.4.s5, 4.4.k2
- concept: Review network cost with CUR resource-level line items queried in Athena plus VPC Flow Logs to find traffic sources
- refs: 06-management-governance.md, 04-networking-services.md
- hint: Cần biết NAT gateway nào tốn nhất và lưu lượng đi đâu — một nguồn cho dữ liệu chi phí theo resource ID, một nguồn cho luồng mạng.
- status: draft
- created: 2026-10-22
- enriched: 2026-10-22

A company's monthly bill shows a large increase in NAT gateway data processing charges. The company operates NAT gateways in several VPCs across 12 accounts and cannot tell which gateways are responsible or which applications and destinations generate the traffic. The cloud team wants to identify the most expensive NAT gateways and the main sources and destinations of traffic through them before it decides how to optimize, by using managed services and SQL queries. Which combination of actions will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead? (Choose TWO)

- A. Create AWS Budgets cost budgets for each account with alerts at 80 percent so that the account owners investigate their NAT gateway usage
- B. Create an organization-level Cost and Usage Report with resource IDs delivered to Amazon S3 and query the NAT gateway line items with Athena
- C. Enable AWS CloudTrail data events for Amazon S3 and query them to find the instances that are the source or destination of traffic through the NAT gateways
- D. Use AWS Compute Optimizer recommendations to right-size each NAT gateway according to its data processing charges
- E. Enable VPC Flow Logs for the NAT gateways' network interfaces, deliver them to Amazon S3, and query the top source and destination addresses with Athena

**Answer:** B, E

**Explanation:** The Cost and Usage Report is the most detailed cost dataset and, with resource IDs, shows the charge per NAT gateway. Flow Logs record the traffic through the gateway interfaces, so Athena queries reveal who sends data and where.
- Budgets with alerts: say that spending rose, not which gateway or traffic causes it (giải bài toán khác)
- CloudTrail data events for S3: log S3 object API calls, not network flows (dùng sai tính năng)
- Compute Optimizer for NAT gateways: gives no recommendations for NAT gateways (dùng sai tính năng)
Docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cur/latest/userguide/what-is-cur.html
> 🇻🇳 Rà soát chi phí mạng: CUR (kèm resource ID) + Athena cho chi phí theo NAT gateway, VPC Flow Logs cho nguồn/đích lưu lượng.

## Q ai-20261022-a44-08
- domain: cost
- task: 4.4
- topic: networking
- services: Route 53 Resolver, RAM, Route 53
- tags: hybrid-dns, resolver-endpoints, data-transfer-cost
- difficulty: hard
- skills: 4.4.k7
- concept: Resolver endpoints are billed per ENI-hour, so centralize one outbound endpoint and share forwarding rules through AWS RAM
- refs: 04-networking-services.md
- hint: Mỗi VPC có endpoint Resolver riêng nên tốn phí theo giờ — hãy dùng một endpoint chung và chia sẻ rule cho các VPC khác.
- status: draft
- created: 2026-10-22
- enriched: 2026-10-22
- time: 165

A company has 40 VPCs in 40 accounts of one organization. Each VPC has its own Route 53 Resolver outbound endpoint and a forwarding rule for corp.example.com, which resolves on on-premises DNS servers over Direct Connect. The bill shows high Resolver endpoint charges. The company wants to reduce DNS costs while resolution of corp.example.com keeps working from every VPC, private hosted zones and AWS service names keep resolving as they do today, and operational effort stays low. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose TWO)

- A. Create one outbound endpoint and forwarding rule in a shared-services VPC and delete the per-VPC endpoints
- B. Create an inbound endpoint in each VPC so that on-premises DNS servers can resolve names hosted in the VPCs of the organization, and keep the outbound forwarding rules
- C. Change the DHCP options set of each VPC to use the on-premises DNS servers directly as the sole name servers, replacing the outbound rule
- D. Share the forwarding rule with the organization by using AWS Resource Access Manager and associate it with each of the 40 VPCs
- E. Create a private hosted zone for corp.example.com in each VPC instead of the forwarding rule and copy the on-premises records into every zone

**Answer:** A, D

**Explanation:** Resolver endpoints are billed per network interface and hour, so one outbound endpoint replaces forty. A rule shared through AWS RAM and associated with each VPC sends queries through it.
- Inbound endpoints in each VPC: serve queries from on-premises to AWS, the opposite direction, and add charges (giải bài toán khác)
- On-premises DNS servers as sole name servers: private hosted zones and AWS names would stop resolving as today (vi phạm ràng buộc)
- Copied records in private hosted zones: forty copies that drift from the source (tốn vận hành hơn)
Docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/resolver-rules-managing.html
> 🇻🇳 Giảm phí Resolver endpoint: một outbound endpoint dùng chung + chia sẻ forwarding rule qua AWS RAM cho các VPC.

## Q ai-20261022-a44-03
- domain: cost
- task: 4.4
- topic: networking
- services: NLB, ELB
- tags: elb-features, cross-zone, data-transfer-cost
- difficulty: hard
- skills: 4.4.k3, 4.4.s3
- concept: Enabling cross-zone load balancing on an NLB incurs inter-AZ data transfer charges; disabling it keeps traffic within each AZ
- refs: 04-networking-services.md
- hint: Chi phí truyền dữ liệu giữa các AZ tăng vì NLB đang bật cross-zone — thiết lập nào giữ lưu lượng trong từng AZ mà không bỏ AZ nào?
- status: draft
- created: 2026-10-22
- enriched: 2026-10-22
- time: 140

A gaming company runs a TCP-based matchmaking service behind an internet-facing Network Load Balancer that has cross-zone load balancing enabled. The targets are EC2 instances spread evenly across three Availability Zones by an Auto Scaling group, and clients are distributed evenly across the three zonal addresses of the load balancer. The monthly bill shows significant inter-AZ data transfer charges for the service. The company must keep using all three zones for availability, keep the NLB and the TCP protocol, and avoid code changes. Which solution will reduce the data transfer charges MOST cost-effectively?

- A. Replace the Network Load Balancer with an Application Load Balancer, keep cross-zone load balancing enabled, and register the same instances as targets
- B. Turn off cross-zone load balancing and keep the group balanced across the three zones so that each zone has enough targets
- C. Deregister the targets in two of the zones, keep cross-zone load balancing enabled, and let the Auto Scaling group serve every connection from one zone
- D. Put AWS Global Accelerator in front of the load balancer, keep cross-zone load balancing enabled, and let clients enter the AWS network closer to the targets

**Answer:** B

**Explanation:** With cross-zone enabled, an NLB node forwards to targets in other zones and EC2 data transfer charges apply. Disabled, each node serves only its own zone, so balanced capacity per zone removes cross-AZ traffic while all zones stay in use.
- Application Load Balancer: handles HTTP and HTTPS, not the custom TCP protocol (vi phạm ràng buộc)
- Targets in a single zone: removes the multi-zone availability required (vi phạm ràng buộc)
- Global Accelerator: does not change forwarding between zones, and adds charges (giải bài toán khác)
Docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/network/edit-target-group-attributes.html#target-group-cross-zone
> 🇻🇳 NLB bật cross-zone → tính phí truyền dữ liệu giữa AZ; tắt cross-zone và cân bằng số target mỗi AZ để giảm chi phí.

## Q ai-20261022-a13-03
- domain: secure
- task: 1.3
- topic: security
- services: KMS, S3, Organizations
- tags: cross-account-access, sse-kms, iam-policies
- difficulty: hard
- skills: 1.3.s4, 1.3.k1
- concept: Org-wide key sharing with aws:PrincipalOrgID plus kms:ViaService limits use to S3 without per-account policy edits
- refs: 05-security-services.md, B-bao-mat-compliance.md
- hint: Cần ba điều cùng lúc: mọi tài khoản trong tổ chức (kể cả tài khoản mới), chỉ qua S3, và không sửa key policy mỗi lần thêm tài khoản.
- status: draft
- created: 2026-10-22
- enriched: 2026-10-22
- time: 145

A central security account owns a customer managed KMS key that encrypts objects in Amazon S3 buckets across the 70 accounts of an AWS Organization. New accounts join every month. Principals in member accounts must be able to use the key when they access S3 objects with SSE-KMS, but must not be able to call AWS KMS directly to decrypt data. The solution must not require a key policy change when an account is added. Which key policy design meets these requirements?

- A. Allow Principal "*" for the KMS actions that Amazon S3 needs, with a single condition that aws:PrincipalOrgID matches the ID of the organization and no other restriction
- B. List the root principal of every member account in the key policy and add each new account to that list at the time the account joins the organization
- C. Allow Principal "*" for the KMS actions that Amazon S3 needs, with conditions that aws:PrincipalOrgID matches the organization ID and kms:ViaService matches the S3 endpoint of the key's Region
- D. Allow Principal "*" for the KMS actions that Amazon S3 needs, with a single condition that kms:ViaService matches the S3 endpoint of the key's Region and no other restriction

**Answer:** C

**Explanation:** The organization condition admits every current and future member account, and kms:ViaService limits use to requests made by S3 on the principal's behalf; member-account IAM policies still decide who may use S3.
- Organization condition only: principals could call AWS KMS directly (vi phạm ràng buộc).
- Root of every account in the key policy: needs a policy change for each new account (vi phạm ràng buộc).
- ViaService only: any AWS account's principals could use the key through S3 (đặt sai chỗ).
Docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/conditions-kms.html
> 🇻🇳 Dùng aws:PrincipalOrgID (cả tổ chức) kết hợp kms:ViaService (chỉ qua S3) trong key policy — không cần sửa khi thêm account.

## Q ai-20261022-a13-17
- domain: secure
- task: 1.3
- topic: storage
- services: S3
- tags: s3-lifecycle, s3-versioning, compliance
- difficulty: hard
- skills: 1.3.k3, 1.3.s6
- concept: In a versioned bucket a lifecycle expiration only adds a delete marker; permanent deletion also needs noncurrent version expiration
- refs: 02-storage-services.md
- hint: Trong bucket bật versioning, hết hạn bản hiện tại chỉ tạo delete marker — bản cũ vẫn còn nếu không có quy tắc cho nó.
- family: s3-retention-and-deletion
- status: draft
- created: 2026-10-22
- enriched: 2026-10-22
- time: 120

A mortgage lender stores signed loan documents in a new Amazon S3 bucket that has versioning enabled. Documents are uploaded once under unique keys and are never overwritten. Company policy sets a seven-year life for each document. Each document must be deleted automatically seven years after upload, and no protection is required before then. Which solution will meet this requirement with the LEAST operational overhead?

- A. Enable Object Lock in compliance mode with a default retention of seven years on the bucket
- B. Enable Object Lock in governance mode with a default retention of seven years and grant s3:BypassGovernanceRetention to the compliance team
- C. Add an S3 Lifecycle rule that expires current versions after seven years and permanently deletes noncurrent versions as soon as they become noncurrent
- D. Turn on MFA delete for the bucket and require the root user's MFA device whenever a version is deleted permanently

**Answer:** C

**Explanation:** In a versioned bucket, expiring the current version only adds a delete marker. Adding noncurrent version expiration permanently removes the original version, so the document is actually deleted with no manual work.
- Object Lock in either mode: only prevents deletion until retention ends; nothing deletes the data afterwards (giải bài toán khác).
- MFA delete: adds manual friction to deletions and never schedules them (giải bài toán khác).
Docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/lifecycle-expire-general-considerations.html
> 🇻🇳 Xoá tự động sau 7 năm trong bucket versioning → lifecycle expire bản hiện tại + xoá vĩnh viễn noncurrent version; Object Lock chỉ chặn xoá.

## Q ai-20261022-a13-27
- domain: secure
- task: 1.3
- topic: storage
- services: S3, VPC Endpoint
- tags: s3-access-points, iam-policies, least-privilege
- difficulty: medium
- skills: 1.3.s6, 1.3.k1
- concept: S3 Access Points give each team a dedicated policy and optional VPC restriction, replacing an ever-growing bucket policy
- refs: 02-storage-services.md
- hint: Mỗi nhóm cần chính sách và ràng buộc mạng riêng trên cùng một bucket dùng chung — endpoint truy cập nào mang policy riêng?
- status: draft
- created: 2026-10-22
- enriched: 2026-10-22
- time: 115

A data platform team keeps a shared data lake in one Amazon S3 bucket with prefixes for 40 analytics teams. The bucket policy has grown so large that it is hard to review. Each team must be restricted to its own prefix, and some teams must be reachable from their own VPC alone. The company wants to simplify access management without moving the data or changing the bucket's location. Which solution will meet these requirements?

- A. Create an S3 access point per team with its own policy and VPC restriction, and delegate access control from the bucket policy to them
- B. Create a separate bucket for each team, replicate each team's prefix into it with S3 Replication, and apply the VPC restriction per bucket
- C. Use ACLs on every object so that each team owns its objects, and add the network rules and the restriction to the ACLs
- D. Create one gateway VPC endpoint per team and add a statement for each endpoint to the existing bucket policy as a restriction

**Answer:** A

**Explanation:** Each access point enforces its own policy and can accept requests only from a VPC, while the bucket policy just delegates, so permissions scale per team without moving data.
- Separate buckets with replication: moves data and duplicates storage (vi phạm ràng buộc).
- Per-object ACLs: ACLs are disabled by default and cannot express network rules (dùng sai tính năng).
- Endpoint statements in the bucket policy: makes the large policy larger (tốn vận hành hơn).
Docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/access-points.html
> 🇻🇳 Bucket dùng chung nhiều nhóm → S3 Access Points (policy + giới hạn VPC riêng) và uỷ quyền từ bucket policy.

A company keeps a central data lake in an Amazon S3 bucket owned by a data platform account in AWS Organizations. About 150 analytics accounts in the same organization read from the bucket through application roles, and new analytics accounts are created every week. The data must never be readable by principals outside the company. Which solution will meet these requirements and give the data platform team the TIGHTEST control over exactly which roles can read the data?

- A. Add a bucket policy statement that allows read access to principals of the organization through aws:PrincipalOrgID, and let each account grant access to its own roles
- B. Add a bucket policy statement that lists the ARN of every approved analytics role as a principal, and update the statement whenever a role needs access
- C. Create an IAM user in the data platform account for every analytics account of the organization and share its access keys with that account's administrators through AWS Secrets Manager
- D. Enable S3 ACLs on the bucket and grant READ permission to the canonical user ID of each analytics account so that its roles can read, then remove the bucket policy

**Answer:** B

**Explanation:** Naming each approved role in the bucket policy means only those roles can be granted access, whatever an account administrator attaches in their own account, the tightest least-privilege control at the resource.
- Organization-wide condition: any role in the organization can be granted access by its own administrator (giải bài toán khác)
- IAM users with shared keys: long-term credentials, with per-account rather than per-role control (vi phạm ràng buộc)
- S3 ACLs per canonical user ID: grants to whole accounts, and ACLs are disabled by default (dùng sai tính năng)

A company runs 60 projects in one AWS account. Each project team may start, stop and tag only the Amazon EC2 instances that belong to its own project. Engineers sign in through IAM Identity Center, and new projects are created every week. The security team wants to avoid writing and updating a separate IAM policy for every project. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose TWO)

- A. Create one identity policy that allows the EC2 actions only when the Project tag on the instance equals the Project tag of the calling principal
- B. Create a customer managed identity policy for each project that lists the ARNs of the instances that carry the project's tag and attach it to the project's group
- C. Create a permissions boundary for each project that lists the project's instance IDs and attach it to the identity of every engineer
- D. Attach a resource-based policy to each EC2 instance that names the engineer roles allowed to manage it
- E. Tag every instance with a Project tag and pass each engineer's project to the session as an attribute for access control

**Answer:** A, E

**Explanation:** Attribute-based access control compares the Project tag of the resource with the Project tag of the principal in one policy, and Identity Center passes the engineer's project attribute into the session, so a new project needs only correct tags and no new policy.
- One policy per project: a new policy to create and attach each week (tốn vận hành hơn)
- Boundary per project: same per-project maintenance, and boundaries only cap permissions (tốn vận hành hơn)
- Resource-based policy on instances: EC2 instances do not support resource-based policies (cấu hình không tồn tại)
Docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/introduction_attribute-based-access-control.html
> 🇻🇳 Nhiều dự án, thêm liên tục → ABAC: một policy so khớp aws:PrincipalTag với thẻ tài nguyên.

## Q ai-20261022-a11-20
- domain: secure
- task: 1.1
- topic: management
- services: Organizations
- tags: scp, allow-list, multi-account
- difficulty: hard
- skills: 1.1.s4, 1.1.k1
- concept: An SCP allow list works only when FullAWSAccess is replaced at that level; deny lists leave future services open
- refs: 06-management-governance.md
- hint: FullAWSAccess vẫn gắn ở cấp OU thì allow-list không có tác dụng — cần thay thế chứ không chỉ thêm SCP.
- status: draft
- created: 2026-10-22
- enriched: 2026-10-22
- time: 160

A company has 20 sandbox accounts in a Sandbox OU. The sandbox accounts must be able to use only Amazon EC2, Amazon S3 and AWS Lambda, and no other AWS service, including services that AWS launches in the future, even if a sandbox administrator attaches AdministratorAccess to a user. The organization has all features enabled, and the default FullAWSAccess SCP is attached to the root, the Sandbox OU and every account. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose TWO)

- A. Create a permissions boundary that allows the three services and attach it to each sandbox administrator
- B. Create an SCP that allows only the ec2:*, s3:* and lambda:* actions and attach it to the Sandbox OU for the 20 sandbox accounts
- C. Attach the new SCP to the management account, keeping FullAWSAccess in place, so that it restricts the sandbox accounts through the hierarchy
- D. Create an SCP that denies every other AWS service by name, leaving EC2, S3 and Lambda untouched, and attach it to the Sandbox OU
- E. Detach the FullAWSAccess SCP from the Sandbox OU so that the allow list is the only policy granting access at that level

**Answer:** B, E

**Explanation:** For an allow list, an Allow for the three services must exist at every level and FullAWSAccess must be removed where the list is applied, or the OU still allows everything. As an SCP, it caps even an AdministratorAccess user.
- Permissions boundary per administrator: covers only identities that carry it (tốn vận hành hơn)
- SCP on the management account: SCPs do not affect the management account or other accounts through it (đặt sai chỗ)
- Deny list by service name: services launched later are not denied (vi phạm ràng buộc)
Docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_scps_evaluation.html
> 🇻🇳 Allow-list SCP: gỡ FullAWSAccess ở cấp đó và gắn SCP chỉ cho phép dịch vụ cần dùng; deny-list bỏ sót dịch vụ mới.

## Q ai-20261022-a11-23
- domain: secure
- task: 1.1
- topic: security
- services: S3, SQS, IAM
- tags: resource-based-policies, confused-deputy
- difficulty: hard
- skills: 1.1.s5
- concept: S3 event notifications to SQS use the queue's resource policy for the S3 service principal, scoped with aws:SourceArn and aws:SourceAccount
- refs: 05-security-services.md, 07-application-integration.md
- hint: S3 gửi thông báo vào SQS dựa trên chính sách của hàng đợi, không phải role — và phải giới hạn đúng một bucket để tránh confused deputy.
- status: draft
- created: 2026-10-22
- enriched: 2026-10-22
- time: 135

A company configures Amazon S3 event notifications so that a bucket sends messages to an Amazon SQS queue in the same account. The configuration fails validation because the queue's access policy has no statements. The security team also requires that only this specific bucket can send messages to the queue, and that buckets in other accounts cannot use the queue even if they name it as a destination. Which solution will meet these requirements?

- A. Attach an identity policy to the IAM user who configures the notification that allows sqs:SendMessage on the queue, and let S3 use that user's permissions at delivery time
- B. Create an IAM role that allows sqs:SendMessage and name the role as the notification role in the bucket's notification configuration so S3 assumes it
- C. Add a statement to the queue's access policy that allows the s3.amazonaws.com service principal to call sqs:SendMessage, with aws:SourceArn and aws:SourceAccount conditions
- D. Add a statement to the queue's access policy that allows the s3.amazonaws.com service principal to call sqs:SendMessage on the queue without adding any conditions

**Answer:** C

**Explanation:** S3 delivers notifications as a service principal, so the destination queue's resource-based policy must allow it. The aws:SourceArn and aws:SourceAccount conditions restrict delivery to this bucket and account and prevent the confused deputy problem.
- Identity policy for the configuring user: the user's permissions are not used when S3 delivers messages (dùng sai tính năng)
- Notification role: S3 notifications to SQS have no role setting (cấu hình không tồn tại)
- Service principal without conditions: any bucket, including other accounts', could send to the queue (vi phạm ràng buộc)
Docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/grant-destinations-permissions-to-s3.html
> 🇻🇳 S3 → SQS: queue policy cho principal s3.amazonaws.com + điều kiện aws:SourceArn/SourceAccount để chống confused deputy.

## Q ai-20261022-a12-10
- domain: secure
- task: 1.2
- topic: networking
- services: Site-to-Site VPN, Direct Connect, Client VPN
- tags: dx-resiliency
- difficulty: medium
- skills: 1.2.s4
- concept: Private IP VPN over a Direct Connect transit virtual interface gives IPsec encryption and an end-to-end private path
- refs: 04-networking-services.md
- hint: Mã hoá IPsec mà vẫn không đi qua internet và không dùng IP public — kết hợp nào cho đường riêng đã mã hoá?
- status: draft
- family: hybrid-encrypted-link
- created: 2026-10-22
- enriched: 2026-10-22
- time: 110

A pharmaceutical company must connect its data center to a VPC to exchange clinical-study reports that total a few gigabytes per day. Compliance requires that all traffic between the data center and AWS be encrypted in transit. The company has no existing connectivity to AWS, and its edge routers support IPsec. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST securely?

- A. Create an AWS Client VPN endpoint in the VPC and install the Client VPN software on the servers in the data center to encrypt the traffic in transit
- B. Order an AWS Direct Connect connection and create a private virtual interface to the virtual private gateway of the VPC to carry the traffic privately
- C. Create an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection over the internet between the customer gateway device and the virtual private gateway of the VPC
- D. Order a Direct Connect connection, create a transit virtual interface, and create a private IP Site-to-Site VPN connection attached to a transit gateway

**Answer:** D

**Explanation:** Private IP VPN over a Direct Connect transit virtual interface encrypts traffic with IPsec and keeps it on a private path with no public IP addresses or internet exposure.
- Client VPN on data center servers: per-client tool that does not connect a site (giải bài toán khác)
- Direct Connect with a private virtual interface: private path but no encryption, which compliance requires (vi phạm ràng buộc)
- Site-to-Site VPN over the internet: encrypted, but the tunnels cross the public internet and are more exposed (vi phạm ràng buộc)
Docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpn/latest/s2svpn/private-ip-dx.html
> 🇻🇳 Bảo mật nhất = riêng tư + mã hoá: Direct Connect transit VIF + private IP VPN.

## Q ai-20261022-a12-03
- domain: secure
- task: 1.2
- topic: networking
- services: VPC Endpoint, S3
- tags: s3-block-public-access, iam-policies
- difficulty: hard
- skills: 1.2.k2, 1.2.k3
- concept: A gateway endpoint policy limits which buckets a VPC can reach (exfiltration control); a bucket policy with aws:SourceVpce limits who can reach a bucket
- refs: 04-networking-services.md
- hint: Cần chặn đường ra tới bucket của người khác, không phải chặn người lạ vào bucket của mình — chính sách nào gắn vào endpoint?
- status: draft
- created: 2026-10-22
- enriched: 2026-10-22
- time: 135

A financial firm runs data-processing instances in private subnets. The instances read and write the firm's Amazon S3 buckets through a gateway VPC endpoint. An audit found that a compromised instance could copy data through the same endpoint to an S3 bucket that belongs to an unknown external account. The firm must close this exfiltration path, keep S3 traffic on the AWS network through the endpoint, and avoid adding proxy servers. Which solution will meet these requirements?

- A. Add a bucket policy to each of the firm's buckets that denies requests that do not arrive through the endpoint by using the aws:SourceVpce condition key
- B. Attach a security group to the gateway endpoint that allows outbound HTTPS traffic to the host names of the firm's buckets
- C. Route S3 traffic through a NAT gateway and deploy AWS Network Firewall with a domain allow list that contains the host names of the firm's buckets
- D. Attach an endpoint policy to the gateway endpoint that limits S3 actions to the ARNs of the firm's buckets and their objects

**Answer:** D

**Explanation:** An endpoint policy is evaluated for every request that uses the endpoint, so restricting its resources to the firm's bucket ARNs blocks copies to external buckets while traffic still stays on the AWS network.
- Bucket policy with aws:SourceVpce: protects the firm's buckets from outside callers but does not stop writes to other buckets (giải bài toán khác)
- Security group on the endpoint: gateway endpoints have no security groups (cấu hình không tồn tại)
- NAT gateway plus Network Firewall: abandons the endpoint and adds firewall infrastructure to run (tốn vận hành hơn)
Docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/vpc-endpoints-s3.html
> 🇻🇳 Endpoint policy = bucket nào VPC được truy cập; bucket policy aws:SourceVpce = ai được vào bucket của mình.
